# TrailReplay

> Turn GPS tracks into animated 3D map replays and export them as video. Runs
> entirely in the browser: no account, no upload API, nothing stored on a
> server. Accepts GPX and KML routes, and `.replay` project files.

## For agents

If you are preparing a route for someone — a race with aid stations, a trek with
huts, a route with named climbs — **do not drive the UI**. Build a `.replay`
file and hand it to them to drop on the page. One file carries the routes, the
pins, the names, the colours and the playback settings.

- [Building a .replay file](https://trailreplay.com/replay-file.md): the complete
  format specification, the kilometre-to-coordinate maths, and the pitfalls that
  silently drop pins from the map. Read this before writing anything.
- [make-replay.mjs](https://trailreplay.com/make-replay.mjs): builds a `.replay`
  from a short JSON recipe that anchors things by kilometre. Node built-ins
  only, no install step.
- [example-recipe.json](https://trailreplay.com/example-recipe.json): a real
  race, start to finish, as a recipe.

Opening a file is a drag-and-drop onto <https://trailreplay.com>, done by the
person, not by you.

## About

- [TrailReplay](https://trailreplay.com): the app itself.
- [Tutorial](https://trailreplay.com/tutorial.html): what the app can do.
- [Getting a GPX out of Strava, Garmin, Wikiloc and others](https://trailreplay.com/gpx-download-guide.html)
- [Source](https://github.com/alexalmansa/TrailReplay)
